name: Prague Castle
description: A huge castle complex on the hill above the Vltava, seat of Czech rulers for over a thousand years, including the Old Royal Palace.

name: St Vitus Cathedral
description: The Gothic cathedral inside Prague Castle, where Czech kings were crowned and buried, with a stained-glass window by Alfons Mucha.

name: Old Town Hall and Astronomical Clock
description: The medieval astronomical clock on the Old Town Hall, first installed in 1410. On the hour, figures of the apostles appear in windows above the dials.

name: Old Town Square
description: The main square of the old town, ringed by pastel houses, the Old Town Hall and the twin towers of the Týn Church.

name: Wenceslas Square
description: A long, wide square in the New Town, scene of the mass protests of 1989. A statue of St Wenceslas stands at the top end.

name: Melantrich building
description: A building on Wenceslas Square from whose balcony dissident leaders addressed the crowds during the Velvet Revolution in 1989.

name: Municipal House
description: An Art Nouveau civic building from 1912, next to the Powder Tower, with the Smetana Hall concert hall, a café and a restaurant.

name: New City Hall
description: The early-1900s seat of Prague’s city government, on Mariánské Square, with large sculptures at its corners.

name: Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius
places: Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius, Resslova
description: An Orthodox church where the Czech parachutists who assassinated Reinhard Heydrich hid and died in 1942. Its crypt is now a memorial.

name: Old Jewish Cemetery
description: One of Europe’s oldest Jewish burial grounds, in the Jewish Quarter, with some 12,000 tombstones crowded together, many of them tilting.

name: Old-New Synagogue
description: Europe’s oldest active synagogue, a 13th-century Gothic building in the Jewish Quarter. Legend says the Golem lies in its attic.

name: Estates Theatre
description: An 18th-century theatre in the old town where Mozart’s Don Giovanni premiered in 1787. It still stages opera, drama and ballet.

name: Charles Bridge
description: The 14th-century stone bridge across the Vltava, lined with baroque statues of saints and busy from early morning to late at night.
